title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers a request of the provisioner contract with, application/json, as the integration contract's refusal, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/refusal.schema.json. The codes the adapter that serves a node pool meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking, for each cause that refusal lists, a replay under the replay rule of https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json among them: it tells the adapter nothing about which cause applied, and an adapter never takes it as the access key being revoked; 403 forbidden, a request outside the access key's rights, a claim of a pool the adapter does not serve, and a request naming a dispatch_id that is unknown or that belongs to another adapter, each with the same signed body as an unknown pool, so nobody learns whether an id exists: the adapter's signature and this check authorise a request, not the id, and the control plane decides it before any 409 or 410; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 no_gateway, a claim whose run's pool choice resolves to no gateway; 409 handed_over, a second handover, since a run key is handed over at most once per run; 409 not_dispatched, a handover before dispatched; 409 lease_expired, a dispatched or a handover after the lease lapsed and the dispatch, not yet handed over, went back to the queue with the same run, on which the adapter stops the job it started for that dispatch; 410 gone, a request of a dispatch that ended because its work item was closed or undone; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the adapter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry. A release after the handover is not refused: it is answered as a success, the signed 204, and ends the run. No refusal is tied to a step or to a policy. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the adapter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the adapter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A member this schema does not define is refused.
